content_html: Well said J. I worked on a project recently which served the purpose of being a State Engine for an application. Instead of creating a Mondo State Engine class, with every state and all it’s complexities within, the Engine was simply a broker/manager of individual state classes, each with it’s own behavior. Much more manageable.

How one can distinguish between God Code and AOP/Metadata driven/complex configuration driven code ? Microsoft heavy use of attributes in .Net Framework shows the strength of these techniques. How can one determine if he is making effective use of these techniques or over-engineering?
